newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA SWITCH HORAN TO FLYHALF.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA SWITCH HORAN TO FLYHALF.

text.p: Australia rugby union coach Greg Smith on Sunday moved Tim Horan across the backline to fill the problem flyhalf position for the first test against France later this month.
Smith overlooked the claims of specialist flyhalfs David Knox and Scott Bowen in naming his side for the encounter with the Five Nations champions in Sydney on June 21.
Horan, who has made his reputation with the Wallabies in the centres, played at fullback for Queensland all season in the southern hemisphere provincial Super 12 competition.
His latest position change follows a brief stint on the wing during Australia's tour of Britain last year.
The flyhalf position has proved a headache for Australia since veteran Michael Lynagh retired from test rugby after the 1995 World Cup in South Africa.
Wallaby captain John Eales said Horan would easily adapt to playing at flyhalf despite his lack of experience in the position.
"Tim has played on the wing for Australia and at fullback for Queensland all season and I am sure he can handle the role," Eales said.
Seven ACT Brumbies players, the biggest ever contingent from Canberra in a Wallaby line-up, won selection as a reward for reaching this season's Super 12 final.
The Brumbies, who lost to Auckland in the final, proved the surprise package of the tournament, overshadowing New South Wales and Queensland, Australia's traditional provincial powers.
Prop Ewen McKenzie, a key figure in ACT's success this season, was recalled after a two-year absence from test rugby.
The second and final test against France will be played at Ballymore in Brisbane on June 28.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke (New South Wales), 14-Ben Tune (Queensland), 13-Jason Little (Queensland), 12-Pat Howard (ACT), 11-Joe Roff (ACT), 10-Tim Horan (Queensland), 9-George Gregan (ACT), 8-Daniel Manu (New South Wales), 7-David Wilson (Queensland), 6-Brett Robinson (ACT), 5-John Eales (Queensland, captain), 4-David Giffen (ACT), 3-Ewen McKenzie (ACT), 2-Marco Caputo (ACT), 1-Richard Harry (New South Wales).
Reserves - Stephen Larkham (ACT), Sam Payne (New South Wales), Troy Coker (ACT), Mark Cockbain (Queensland), Dan Crowley (Queensland), Michael Foley (Queensland).
